sutta: We come to 6.12. Thus have I heard. On one occasion, the Blessed One was dwelling at Rajagaha on Mount Vulture's Peak. Not long after Devadatta had left, then when the night had advanced, Brahma Sahampati, of stunning beauty, illuminating the entire Mount Vulture's Peak, approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, referring to Devadatta, he recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One. As its own fruit brings destruction to the plantain, bamboo, and reed, as its as its embryo destroys the mule, so do honors destroy the scoundrel. This is the end of the Sutta. So, plantain plant, is what we call the banana plant. So, when the banana plant gives off the fruit, uh people harvest it and chop down the banana tree. So, the fruit destroys the banana plant. Similarly with bamboo and reed. So, this is uh that honors destroy the scoundrel. Honors, that is fame, is for a monk is very dangerous. That is why later we'll come across one Samyutta, Labha Sakkara Samyutta, which is about gains and fame, now, offerings and uh fame for a monk is extremely dangerous. So, here, because fame, uh Devadatta destroyed himself.
